name: Austin Hatch
headline: Two-time plane crash survivor, former Michigan basketball player and keynote speaker on overcoming adversity.
formats: Keynotes for companies, sales teams, schools, churches and athletic programs, in person or virtual
ctaLabel: Book Austin as your next speaker
summary: Austin Hatch survived two plane crashes, eight years apart, that took his parents and siblings. After the second, in 2011, he spent two months in a coma and relearned how to walk, talk and eat, then went on to play basketball at the University of Michigan on the scholarship it had honored through his recovery. After graduating he worked in Domino's corporate office before turning to speaking full time. His Overcome It keynote teaches the G.R.I.T. framework (growth mindset, resilience, integrity and a team-first mentality) to companies, sales teams, schools and athletic programs.

talks: Overcome It: the G.R.I.T. framework of growth mindset, resilience, integrity and a team-first mentality, for turning adversity into opportunity. Keynote, in person or virtual.
The Secret: why some people and teams overcome adversity and others don't, and how a greater purpose drives grit. Keynote.
Team First: leading by example, following through on commitments and doing common things in an uncommon way. Keynote for companies and sales teams.
Overcome It for Students and Athletes: grit, resilience and responding to setbacks, for schools, churches and athletic programs. Keynote or school assembly.
audiences: Corporate leaders and teams, sales and financial services teams, schools and student-athletes, churches, athletic programs, healthcare organizations
proof: Survived a 2003 plane crash in Wells County, Indiana, at age 8, and a 2011 crash in Charlevoix, Michigan
Spent about two months in a medically induced coma and relearned how to walk, talk and eat
Led Canterbury High School to its first sectional championship (2010–11); News-Sentinel Prep Sports Player of the Year and All-State Honorable Mention
Offered a full University of Michigan basketball scholarship by John Beilein on June 15, 2011; Michigan honored it through his recovery and he signed in 2013
Michigan men's basketball: player, then two seasons as an undergraduate assistant coach; part of two Big Ten Tournament championship teams and an NCAA national runner-up team
Scored his only college point on a free throw, December 23, 2014
Worked in Domino's corporate office after graduating
Creator of the G.R.I.T. framework: Growth mindset, Resilience, Integrity, Team-first mentality
Spoken for teams including Domino's, Nestlé, Northwestern Mutual, MassMutual, Bernstein, loanDepot, FirstService Residential, Farm Bureau Insurance in Michigan and Purdue Men's Basketball
events: Parkview Sports Medicine, Fort Wayne (Nov 2025): student-athletes from 14 high schools, the University of Saint Francis and Indiana Tech
Parkview Health leadership, Parkview Mirro Center, Fort Wayne (Nov 2025)
Schools, corporations and community groups across the country with the Overcome It talk
